stories.title: Government to function as normal while Burnham on holiday
stories.summary: Andy Burnham's government will continue to function normally while the new Prime Minister is on holiday. Downing Street confirmed arrangements are in place to ensure continuity of government during the break.

stories.title: Andy Burnham targets migrant crisis ahead of Macron's visit to No 10
stories.summary: Burnham is preparing to tackle Channel crossings and the broader migrant crisis as French President Macron visits Downing Street. The talks are expected to focus on joint enforcement measures and bilateral cooperation.

stories.title: Burnham to crack down on UK mega-donors influencing politics
stories.summary: The Prime Minister is launching a new taskforce to examine the influence of major political donors, signalling a push for transparency reform in political financing.

topics.name: Burnham Gov Intelligence
topics.description: Procurement, tech/AI, spending, vendor & priority signals

stories.title: 🏗️ Burnham Government Strips Back Procurement Rules to Prioritise British Jobs
stories.summary: The government is replacing wide-ranging procurement criteria to put British jobs and skills at the heart of £90bn in public contracts. Firms bidding for contracts will need to prove they are creating jobs rather than meeting green and social targets.

stories.title: 🤖 Burnham Centralises AI Policy in His Office — DSIT Scrapped, AI Minister at Cabinet Table
stories.summary: PM Burnham appointed Kanishka Narayan as the UK's first Cabinet-level AI minister while abolishing DSIT, redistributing its responsibilities to the new Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (DBIST). Critics warn this creates a 'fractured strategy' for British tech.

stories.title: 🤖 GOV.UK Wallet Opens Sandbox for Digital ID Firms
stories.summary: The Government Digital Service is offering tech companies a new test environment for the GOV.UK Wallet smartphone system, which is designed to store and provide access to state-issued digital ID. This signals a push to advance the UK's digital identity infrastructure.

stories.title: 🤖 Domestic AI Firms Offered £100m Opportunity to Improve Public Services
stories.summary: The government's new Sovereign AI unit has opened a competitive bidding process for UK startups to put forward tech ideas to meet defined public sector challenges, with £100m on offer.

stories.title: 🏗️ Public Sector Procurement to Drive AI Innovation — Chancellor
stories.summary: Chancellor John Healey signalled that public contracts addressing health, national security, cyber resilience, and computing infrastructure will be used to drive domestic AI innovation.

stories.title: 🏢 Phoenix Selected for Ofgem Microsoft Enterprise Licence Renewal
stories.summary: Ofgem has selected Phoenix to handle the provision and renewal of its current Microsoft Enterprise licence, a notable vendor signal in the public sector technology market.

stories.title: 💰 'The Chancellor Is in a Bind': Is No 11 at Odds with Burnham's Big Vision?
stories.summary: Analysis suggests tension between Chancellor Healey's fiscal caution and PM Burnham's ambitious spending plans for reindustrialisation and devolution. Healey is set to argue the UK economy can 'turn a corner' despite bond market concerns.

topics.name: Parliament
topics.description: House of Commons, House of Lords, PMQs, debates, legislation

stories.title: Armed Forces Bill Continues Lords Committee Stage
stories.summary: The House of Lords resumed scrutiny of the Armed Forces Bill in committee this week. The bill is working through the upper house, with peers continuing to examine its provisions in detail.

stories.title: Parliament Returns After Summer Recess
stories.summary: Both Houses returned to business from 1 September 2026, with a full legislative programme ahead. The Commons resumed committee work and early readings of government bills in the first week back.

stories.title: Chancellor to Argue UK Economy Can 'Turn a Corner' Despite Bond Market Turmoil
stories.summary: Chancellor John Healey will make the case that the UK economy is improving despite turbulence in bond markets, detailing plans to spread growth more widely across the UK.

stories.title: Burnham Faces an Impossible Job — But Has a Secret Weapon in Kemi Badenoch
stories.summary: A political sketch piece in the Guardian argues Burnham's governing challenge is immense, but his greatest asset may be a Conservative opposition that continues to struggle under Badenoch's leadership.

stories.title: Kemi Badenoch Delivers Keynote Speech on Defence
stories.summary: Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch gave a keynote speech on defence at a central London event, seeking to position the Tories as a credible force on national security as she marks one year in the leadership role.

stories.title: Tory Leader Faces Fresh Questions After Defending Ex-Neo-Nazi Candidate
stories.summary: Kemi Badenoch faced a difficult week in August after it emerged that a former neo-Nazi activist had been selected as a Conservative candidate in Somerset. Her apparent defence of the individual raised questions about the party's vetting processes.

stories.title: The UK Conservatives Face Problems — Is Their Leader One of Them?
stories.summary: BBC reporting reveals that Conservative insiders are privately describing Kemi Badenoch's recent missteps as a 'total disaster' for the party as it struggles to find its opposition footing against the new Burnham government.

stories.title: UK Must Build Own Nuclear Missiles, Say Lib Dems
stories.summary: The Liberal Democrats have called for the UK to develop its own nuclear missile capability, in a significant shift on defence policy for the party. The announcement came as Ed Davey sought to differentiate the Lib Dems on national security.

stories.title: Ed Davey Calls for Closer EU Reintegration
stories.summary: Liberal Democrat leader Ed Davey has called for more ambitious reintegration with Europe, arguing it brings necessary economic and strategic benefits. The Guardian editorial broadly agreed with the approach.

topics.name: Reform UK
topics.description: Nigel Farage, party news and announcements

stories.title: Reform Suspends Two Senior Officials After Channel 4 Undercover Investigation on Donations
stories.summary: A Channel 4 News undercover investigation alleged that senior Reform UK figures discussed ways to breach foreign donations law. The party suspended its head of policy James Orr and senior Farage aide Dan Jukes pending an investigation.

stories.title: Farage: 'I Wasn't Even Listening' at Donations Scandal Meeting
stories.summary: Nigel Farage sought to distance himself from the donations scandal at his party conference, claiming he was not paying attention during the meeting captured in the undercover footage and that he knows donation law 'better than anybody'.

stories.title: Undercover Report on Donations 'Looks Bad' for Reform, Admits Farage
stories.summary: Farage admitted the undercover report 'looks bad' for Reform UK but insisted the party did nothing illegal, even as questions mounted at the party's annual conference. The scandal dominated coverage of what was supposed to be a key party showcase event.

stories.title: Swinney Sticks with Pledge to Cap Prices on Basic Foods
stories.summary: Scottish First Minister John Swinney reaffirmed the SNP's commitment to capping prices on basic foodstuffs, a flagship policy facing scrutiny over its legal and practical implementation.

stories.title: SNP Secures Fifth Consecutive Term at Holyrood But Faces New Challenges
stories.summary: The SNP won a fifth consecutive term at the 2026 Scottish Parliament election, remaining the largest party despite losing six seats and falling short of an overall majority. Leader John Swinney now faces pressure to manage minority government.

topics.name: Cabinet Office
topics.description: Government reshuffles, senior appointments, cross-department policy

stories.title: Louise Haigh Appointed First Secretary of State and Cabinet Office Minister
stories.summary: The July 2026 ministerial appointments saw Louise Haigh MP take on the roles of First Secretary of State, Chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster, and Minister for the Cabinet Office under PM Burnham — making her the number two in government.

stories.title: New Digital Devolution Programme Begins
stories.summary: A new programme making digital, data and AI skills and services available to local leaders has launched, part of the Burnham government's agenda to extend digital capabilities beyond Whitehall.

topics.name: Elections & By-elections
topics.description: Upcoming or recent election results, polls

stories.title: Farage Wins Clacton By-election Boycotted by Major Parties
stories.summary: Nigel Farage won the Clacton by-election with 22,239 votes, with Count Binface coming second with 9,455. Major Westminster parties boycotted the contest. A parliamentary investigation resumed against Farage shortly after the result.

stories.title: UK Local Election Results 2026 — Reform Sweeps, Labour Holds Ground
stories.summary: The 2026 local elections in England saw Reform UK make sweeping gains. Labour maintained its position in key urban areas, while the Conservatives and Liberal Democrats experienced mixed results.

stories.title: House of Lords (Hereditary Peers) Act 2026 — Reform Enacted
stories.summary: The landmark legislation removing the right of hereditary peers to sit and vote in the House of Lords became law in March 2026. Further reform, including a potential elected upper chamber, remains under discussion.

stories.title: Lords Debate Essential Services and AI as Part of Cyber Bill
stories.summary: The House of Lords debated provisions covering AI and data centre incident reporting as part of the Cyber Security Bill's passage through the upper house, reflecting growing legislative attention to AI governance.

stories.title: Armed Forces Bill Committee Stage Continues in Lords
stories.summary: Peers continued their detailed scrutiny of the Armed Forces Bill during committee stage in the first week of September, with discussion on personnel, welfare and powers provisions.
